# Music of the 70s
> Discover, Explore and Relive the Greatest Decade in Music

Sitemap: https://musicofthe70s.net/sitemap.xml

## Tools
- [70s Decade Wheel](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/70s-decade-wheel): Spin the wheel and land on a year from 1970 to 1979. Discover that year's biggest hit, top artists, and defining moment in music history.
- [70s Mood Song Matcher](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/mood-song-matcher): Answer 3 quick questions and get matched with the perfect 70s song for your mood. Rock, disco, soul, country — there's a 70s song for every feeling.
- [70s Music Trivia Quiz](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/70s-trivia-quiz): Test your 70s music knowledge. 10 questions on rock, disco, soul, country and more — new questions every round.
- [Random 70s Artist Picker](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/random-artist-picker): Spin and discover a random 70s artist or band from 605 verified acts — rock, disco, soul, funk, country, punk and more.
- [Random 70s Song Generator](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/random-70s-song): Spin and discover a random iconic 70s song — artist, year, genre and a direct YouTube search link. Rock, disco, soul, country and more.
- [What Was #1 The Week You Were Born?](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/birthday-number-one): Enter your 1970s birthday and discover what song topped the Billboard Hot 100 the week you were born. Your personal piece of music history.

## Listen
- [70s Music Radio and Jukebox](https://musicofthe70s.net/radio/): Watch and listen to free 70s music on genre radio stations, or browse the full 1,000-song Billboard jukebox from 1970-1979. Disco, soul, rock, country, funk and more.

- [Copacabana Barry Manilow: The Story Behind Lola and Tony](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/copacabana-barry-manilow/): Copacabana Barry Manilow explained: the Rio hotel idea, Lola and Tony, the No. 8 peak, a Grammy and the 1985 TV musical it grew into.
- [Hopelessly Devoted to You: Grease Ballad Written Mid-Shoot](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/hopelessly-devoted-to-you/): Hopelessly Devoted to You: how John Farrar wrote Sandy's Grease ballad mid-shoot, its No. 3 Hot 100 peak, the Oscar loss and Sonia's 1994 cover.
- [I Am Woman by Helen Reddy: The Story Behind the Anthem](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/i-am-woman/): I Am Woman by Helen Reddy explained: who wrote it, the 1972 re-recording, one week at No. 1, a 1973 Grammy and a 2025 registry honor.
- [I Want You Back: Jackson 5's First No. 1, Michael at 11](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/i-want-you-back/): I Want You Back: how The Corporation wrote the Jackson 5's first No. 1 with 11-year-old Michael Jackson on lead, plus its charts, awards and covers.
- [Joy to the World Three Dog Night: The Story Behind the Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/joy-to-the-world-three-dog-night/): Joy to the World Three Dog Night explained: Hoyt Axton's tune, a band that said no, six weeks at No. 1 and the number one song of 1971.
- [Mr. Blue Sky: How ELO Wrote It After Two Weeks of Gloom](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/mr-blue-sky/): Mr. Blue Sky: how Jeff Lynne wrote ELO’s sunny hit in a Swiss chalet, its No. 35 Hot 100 peak, UK top 6 and Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 revival.
- [September Earth Wind and Fire: The No. 8 Hit That Stayed](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/september-earth-wind-and-fire/): September Earth Wind and Fire peaked at No. 8 yet became their anthem. The writers, the 21st night lyric, charts, certifications and covers.
- [Wish You Were Here Pink Floyd: Radio Intro and a Lost Friend](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/wish-you-were-here-pink-floyd/): Wish You Were Here Pink Floyd: the radio-tuned intro, Syd Barrett's 1975 studio visit, Grappelli's buried violin and the album that hit number one.
- [Close to You: Who Recorded It Before the Carpenters](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/close-to-you/): Close to You was cut by Richard Chamberlain, Dionne Warwick and Dusty Springfield first. How the Carpenters made it a 1970 number one.
- [Dreams Fleetwood Mac: Written in 10 Minutes, Alive in 2020](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/dreams-fleetwood-mac/): Dreams Fleetwood Mac took Stevie Nicks 10 minutes to write and one week at number one. How it was recorded and why a 2020 skateboard video revived it.
- [Rocket Man Elton John: The Hit That Peaked at No. 6](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/rocket-man-elton-john/): Rocket Man Elton John never hit number one. See its No. 6 Hot 100 peak, the Bradbury story behind it, and the Shatner and Kate Bush covers.
- [Stairway to Heaven: Every Section of the 8:02 Explained](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/stairway-to-heaven/): Stairway to Heaven, timed section by section: the Welsh cottage, the studios, the Belfast debut, the radio record and the Taurus case.
- [70s Number One Hits: Every Billboard #1, 1970 to 1979](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/70s-number-one-hits/): All 253 70s number one hits on the Billboard Hot 100, from Raindrops to Escape. Sort by weeks at #1, see who ruled the decade, and play each one.
- [70s One Hit Wonders: 147 Verified, One Chart Hit Each](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/70s-one-hit-wonders/): 147 real 70s one hit wonders, verified against this site's own Billboard data and each act's full career chart history. Sortable, with plays.
- [Tragedy Bee Gees: The 1979 Original Behind Steps' Cover](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/tragedy-bee-gees/): Tragedy Bee Gees blended disco with a country chord change in 1979, then Steps sent it back to number one in 1998 with an even bigger seller.
- [Too Much Heaven: The Bee Gees Ballad That Bumped Le Freak](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/too-much-heaven/): Too Much Heaven knocked Le Freak off number one for two weeks in January 1979, and the Bee Gees gave every dollar of it to UNICEF. Here's the real story.
- [How Deep Is Your Love: The Bee Gees Ballad Almost Given Away](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/how-deep-is-your-love/): How Deep Is Your Love was written for Yvonne Elliman, not the Bee Gees themselves. See the real chart run, the Grammy win and the 1983 lawsuit.
- [Living for the City: Stevie Wonder's Grammy-Winning Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/living-for-the-city/): Living for the City hit #8, not #45. See Stevie Wonder's real chart peak, the Grammy it won, and the voices behind its spoken-word story.
- [Heartache Tonight: The Eagles' Last Trip to Number One](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/heartache-tonight/): Heartache Tonight gave the Eagles their fifth and final Billboard #1. See how a phone call with Bob Seger built the chorus in minutes.
- [MacArthur Park Donna Summer: Her First Number One Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/macarthur-park-donna-summer/): MacArthur Park Donna Summer turned a 1968 Jimmy Webb ballad into a 17-minute disco suite, and her real first Hot 100 number one, not her third.
- [Night Fever: The Bee Gees Song That Renamed a Movie](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/night-fever/): Night Fever gave Saturday Night Fever its own title. The Bee Gees song spent eight weeks at #1 on the Hot 100 and won a Grammy along the way.
- [The Name of the Game ABBA: The Unfinished Film Song](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/the-name-of-the-game-abba/): The Name of the Game ABBA started as an unfinished film cue called A Bit of Myself. See how it became a UK #1 and a US near-miss in 1977-78.
- [Sir Duke Stevie Wonder: The Tribute That Topped the Charts](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/sir-duke-stevie-wonder/): Sir Duke Stevie Wonder honored Duke Ellington and hit #1. The chart-verified story behind the Songs in the Key of Life classic.
- [Last Dance: The Song That Won Donna Summer Her First Grammy](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/last-dance/): Last Dance won Donna Summer an Oscar, a Golden Globe and her first Grammy from one movie cue. The chart-verified story behind 1978's biggest hit.
- [New Kid in Town: The Eagles' Song About Being Replaced](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/new-kid-in-town/): New Kid in Town gave the Eagles their first Hotel California hit, written after seeing Bruce Springsteen and built on the fear of being replaced.
- [You Should Be Dancing: Where Barry Gibb's Falsetto Began](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/you-should-be-dancing/): You Should Be Dancing gave Barry Gibb his first falsetto lead and the Bee Gees a disco #1, with a surprise cameo from Stephen Stills on timbales.
- [Take a Chance on Me: ABBA's Jogging-Born #1 Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/take-a-chance-on-me/): Take a Chance on Me hit #1 in the UK and #3 in the US. The real story behind ABBA's jogging-born title and its grueling 40-track vocal session.
- [Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain: Nelson's First No. 1](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/blue-eyes-crying-in-the-rain/): Blue Eyes Crying in the Rain gave Willie Nelson his first number one as a performer in 1975, a Fred Rose cover Columbia nearly rejected as a demo.
- [Flash Light Parliament: The Bass Line That Wasn't a Bass](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/flash-light-parliament/): Flash Light Parliament built its famous bass line on three chained Minimoog synths, not a bass guitar, and rode it to Casablanca's first R&B No. 1.
- [In the Navy Village People: The Song the Navy Almost Used](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/in-the-navy-village-people/): In the Navy Village People peaked at #3 on the Hot 100 in 1979, the disco hit the real US Navy almost used for recruitment before backing out.
- [Time in a Bottle Jim Croce: The Number One He Never Heard](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/time-in-a-bottle-jim-croce/): Time in a Bottle Jim Croce wrote in 1970 for his unborn son became his second number one, three months after he died. The real chart story.
- [Bad Girls: The Donna Summer Hit a Police Stop Inspired](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/bad-girls/): Bad Girls held number one for five weeks in 1979. The real Sunset Boulevard incident that inspired Donna Summer's biggest Hot 100 hit, verified.
- [I Will Always Love You Dolly Parton: She Said No to Elvis](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/i-will-always-love-you-dolly-parton/): I Will Always Love You Dolly Parton wrote in 1973 hit #1 country twice. In between, she turned down Elvis Presley's manager. The real chart story.
- [Marvin Gaye Let's Get It On: A Number One That Got Bumped](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/marvin-gaye-lets-get-it-on/): Marvin Gaye Let's Get It On hit number one twice in September 1973, interrupted by Helen Reddy. The real songwriting and chart story, verified.
- [You Are the Sunshine of My Life: Written After the Divorce](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/you-are-the-sunshine-of-my-life/): You Are the Sunshine of My Life hit #1 in 1973, recorded the same summer Stevie Wonder's marriage to Syreeta Wright ended. The real story, chart-verified.
- [ABBA Knowing Me Knowing You: A #1 in Five Countries](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/abba-knowing-me-knowing-you/): ABBA Knowing Me Knowing You topped the charts in five countries in 1977, but stalled at number 14 in the US. The real chart and studio story.
- [Al Green Tired of Being Alone: The Fifth-Try Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/al-green-tired-of-being-alone/): Al Green Tired of Being Alone reached number 11 in 1971, but four earlier singles from the same album missed first. The real writing and chart story.
- [Best of My Love: The Number One the Eagles Didn't Want](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/best-of-my-love/): Best of My Love gave the Eagles their first number one in 1975, a soft country ballad the band and their own label almost buried first.
- [Jive Talkin: The Bridge Sound That Rebuilt the Bee Gees](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/jive-talkin/): Jive Talkin came from tires on a Miami bridge and a misheard word. It ended a four-year US chart drought for the Bee Gees in 1975.
- [Somebody to Love: The Song Freddie Mercury Wrote Alone](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/somebody-to-love/): Somebody to Love was Freddie Mercury's solo composition, built to sound like a 100-voice gospel choir from three singers. Real 1976 chart data inside.
- [Give Up the Funk Parliament: A Chorus Sampled 700+ Times](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/give-up-the-funk-parliament/): Give up the funk Parliament turned a three-part jazz structure into a Gold single, then became one of hip-hop's most sampled tracks ever.
- [You and I Rick James: Three Charts, One 8-Minute Song](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/you-and-i-rick-james/): You and I Rick James recorded as an 8:04 studio jam, then cut to 3:08 for radio. It still hit the Hot 100, R&amp;B, and disco charts at once.
- [Georgia on My Mind: Willie Nelson's Surprise No. 1](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/georgia-on-my-mind/): Georgia on My Mind gave Willie Nelson a country number one from an album Columbia didn't want him to make. Here's the real Stardust story.
- [James Brown Get on the Good Foot: Birth of Breakdancing](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/james-brown-get-on-the-good-foot/): James Brown Get on the Good Foot hit #18 in 1972, went gold, and sparked the dance that became breakdancing. The real chart and dance history.
- [Song YMCA: The Studio Question That Built a Disco Anthem](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/song-ymca/): Song YMCA started with a producer who didn't know what the letters meant, then went on to a National Recording Registry induction decades later.
- [Bad Bad Leroy Brown: The Only Number One Jim Croce Saw Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/bad-bad-leroy-brown/): Bad Bad Leroy Brown topped the Hot 100 for two weeks in July 1973, the only number one Jim Croce lived to see before his death that September.
- [Carole King It's Too Late: Written by a Total Stranger](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/carole-king-its-too-late/): Carole King It's Too Late spent five weeks at number one in 1971, but a poet she barely knew wrote its breakup lyrics in a single day.
- [Jolene: The Chart Record It Finally Broke, 52 Years Later](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/jolene/): Jolene peaked at #60 in 1974. Fifty-two years later, after Dolly Parton's death, it finally broke the Billboard Top 40.
- [Superstition Stevie Wonder: The Hit He Tried to Give Away](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/superstition-stevie-wonder/): Superstition Stevie Wonder wrote as a favor for Jeff Beck. Motown kept it instead, and it became his first Grammy-winning number one.
- [Donna Summer Hot Stuff: The Rock Turn That Won a Grammy](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/donna-summer-hot-stuff/): Donna Summer Hot Stuff hit number one, lost it to the Bee Gees, then took it back. The $35 guitar and Grammy story behind the 1979 disco-rock hit.
- [What's Going On Marvin Gaye: The Accidents That Made It](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/whats-going-on-marvin-gaye/): What's Going On Marvin Gaye built into a classic began as a Four Tops reject. A warm-up sax take, a mixing slip, and a bassist on the floor did the rest.
- [Al Green Let's Stay Together: The Song He Didn't Want to Cut](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/al-green-lets-stay-together/): Al Green Let's Stay Together topped the pop chart for one week and the soul chart for nine. Green argued for two days before he would record it.
- [Killer Queen: Freddie Mercury's First Real US Hit](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/killer-queen/): Killer Queen was Freddie Mercury's deliberate bid for a pop hit, a call girl character study that finally broke Queen in America.
- [One of These Nights: The Eagles' Turn Away From Country](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/one-of-these-nights/): One of These Nights gave the Eagles a second number one and their first chart-topping album, then the lineup that recorded it fell apart.
- [ABBA Waterloo: The Song Written to Win, Not to Chart](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/abba-waterloo/): The real story behind ABBA Waterloo: the scrapped title, the tax law behind the costumes, and the Eurovision rule that let them sing in English.
- [How Can You Mend a Broken Heart: Written in Under an Hour](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/how-can-you-mend-a-broken-heart/): How Can You Mend a Broken Heart, the Bee Gees' first US number one, was written in an hour and never even charted in Britain.
- [Bridge Over Troubled Water: The Gospel Line Simon Paid For](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/bridge-over-troubled-water/): Bridge over troubled water hit #1 for six weeks in 1970. Paul Simon borrowed its title from a gospel song, then paid the singer $1,000 for it.
- [I Will Survive: A B-Side Nobody Wanted to Release](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/i-will-survive/): I will survive was a B-side the label refused to push, written by a songwriter who'd just been fired, recorded by a singer healing from spinal surgery.
- [Seasons in the Sun: The Beach Boys Killed It First](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/seasons-in-the-sun/): Seasons in the sun started as a dark French song about a dying, betrayed man. The Beach Boys recorded it, scrapped it, and called it too wimpy to keep.
- [Stayin Alive: Built on a Magazine Story That Was Fake](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/stayin-alive/): Stayin alive was written for a movie based on a magazine article its own writer later admitted he made up. Now doctors use it to teach CPR.
- [We Will Rock You: How Queen Built a Stadium Chant](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/we-will-rock-you/): The real story behind We Will Rock You: the crowd that inspired it, the drum-riser recording trick, and how Queen built rock's biggest stadium chant.
- [Gimme Gimme Gimme: The ABBA Song America Never Got](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/gimme-gimme-gimme/): Gimme Gimme Gimme hit number one in five countries in 1979. Atlantic Records canceled its US single release outright. Here's the real reason why.
- [Mamma Mia Song: The Story ABBA Almost Gave Away](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/mamma-mia-song/): The mamma mia song almost went to another band, then knocked Bohemian Rhapsody off the UK's number one spot. Its real US peak tells a different story.
- [Take It Easy: The Song Jackson Browne Couldn't Finish](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/take-it-easy/): Take it easy started as Jackson Browne's unfinished song. Glenn Frey completed it, and one line built a real park in Winslow, Arizona.
- [Dancing Queen: The Song ABBA Played for a King First](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/dancing-queen/): Discover the real story behind Dancing Queen: the secret royal wedding premiere, the year-long wait, and how it became ABBA's only US #1.
- [Hotel California: What It Really Means (And What It Doesn't)](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/hotel-california/): Discover the real story behind Hotel California: what Don Henley actually says it means, and why the Satanism theories are wrong.
- [Bohemian Rhapsody: The Song Nobody Wanted to Release](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/bohemian-rhapsody/): Discover the real story behind Bohemian Rhapsody: the label that refused it, the DJ who leaked it, and the four hours that made the video.
- [Don McLean American Pie: The Real Story Behind It](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/don-mclean-american-pie/): Discover the real story behind Don McLean American Pie: the 1959 plane crash, the joke he told for decades, and what he finally revealed.
- [Best Songs of the 70s: The Ultimate Decade Ranking](https://musicofthe70s.net/blog/songs/best-songs-of-the-70s/): The 100 best songs of the 70s, ranked by actual year-end Billboard chart position, 1970 to 1979. Sort by song, artist or year, and play each one.

## About
- [About Music of the 70s](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/about): Music of the 70s is a free interactive resource dedicated to the greatest decade in popular music — 1970 to 1979.
- [About the Author](https://musicofthe70s.net/about/author/): Meet Charlie, the writer behind Music of the 70s: a retired content strategist in Blackfalds, Alberta who researches and writes every article on the site.
- [How We Research and Write (Methodology)](https://musicofthe70s.net/about/methodology/): How Music of the 70s checks facts, writes articles and picks songs for its lists: the sources used, the role of AI tools, and how corrections work.
- [Contact](https://musicofthe70s.net/pages/contact): How to reach Music of the 70s with corrections, licensing questions, or feedback on the site's tools.
